subject: ClearWave inference requirements — technical debrief & next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Liao <anna@clearwave.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: ClearWave inference requirements — technical debrief & next steps

Hi Anna — thanks again for the conversation earlier today. Short recap and the technical items we discussed so engineering can prep for the deep-dive workshop. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- Visible latency spikes during your 11:00–13:00 PST peak window (tail p99 > 500ms, impacting user experience).
- Cost sensitivity on inference spend during burst windows; need predictable unit economics.
- Occasional model degradations when long context (>6k tokens) is used for RAG flows.

Stated goals / target SLOs (as we heard):
- Interactive chat p95 latency target: <= 150 ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Retrieval-augmented flows: p95 <= 500 ms for typical 4–8k contexts, p99 graceful degradation.
- Sustained concurrency target: 200 requests/sec with provisioned headroom for 2x bursts.
- Availability: target 99.9% for production endpoints.

Model & data requirements:
- Preference for open/Redwood-verified models (cost + auditability).
- Need 8k+ context support for RAG use cases; evaluation of both 13B int8 and 70B quantized variants.
- Sensitive data (PII) must remain in US regions; audit logs required for compliance.

Initial topology recommendation (high level):
- Dedicated Redwood pool in us-west-2 (reserved baseline capacity) + autoscale for burst to pre-warmed nodes.
- Multi-variant routing: quantized 13B (int8) as primary low-latency path; 70B quantized for high-quality RAG tasks and as fallback.
- KV/prefix caching for common prompts and retrieval outputs to reduce token compute.
- Canary deploys + model fallback policy to ensure graceful degradation.

Attachments: I attached a mutual action plan + a sizing estimate that encodes the preliminary capacity model.

Next steps we agreed:
1) Engineering deep-dive: 90-minute workshop (we propose next Wed, Nov 18) — Diego + Marissa + your eng leads.
2) Redwood to provide a revised sizing estimate and cost delta for the two model profiles (attached).
3) Security/compliance touchpoint — sample audit/log capabilities and data residency checklist.

If this matches your notes, we'll lock the workshop time and share a pre-read.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — that is very close to what we captured. A few clarifications from the eng team: 

- The p95 <= 150 ms target applies to our shortest-turn chat (non-RAG) flows only — for RAG with a full 8k context we expect longer latencies and we can accept up to ~500 ms p95 as you noted.
- Bursts are often sustained for ~10 minutes during business hours; we'd like to see a cost model that accounts for 10–15 minute sustained bursts rather than just short spikes.
- We will need a short write-up on how you handle PII/token redaction and your audit log retention windows (our security team asked for an initial doc).

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to complete evaluation and vendor selection by the end of Q1 2027, with a pilot in Q2. There is a vendor security questionnaire we will share — can your security/ops team fill that out?

We are available for the deep-dive next Wed (Nov 18), 09:00–10:30 PT. Please confirm attendees and we will share a small sample load profile (I attached a JSON snippet).

Best,
Anna
Director, Product & ML — ClearWave

Redwood proposed execution plan (high level):
- Architecture: Dedicated pool (us-west-2) with 6 reserved GPUs for baseline + autoscale to additional pre-warmed nodes for bursts. We will configure a hot path to the quantized 13B model for low-latency chat and route RAG queries to the quantized 70B when retrieval confidence or prompt length demands it.
- Caching & batching: Implement prefix/KV caching and dynamic batching with workload-aware latency SLOs to preserve p95.
- Fallback policy: If 70B latency exceeds target or capacity is constrained, we will fall back to 13B with a degradation policy that preserves semantics.
- Security/compliance: we will provide a short audit-pack (SOC2 scope, encryption at rest, KMS integration options).

Attachments included: sizing_estimate_v2.csv (cost + capacity scenarios), redwood_mutual_action_plan.docx (M.A.P. with owners).

Action items & owners:
A1) Redwood: run capacity simulation for the attached load profile and share delta-cost scenarios (Diego, Marissa) — due Nov 16.
A2) ClearWave: share vendor security questionnaire and final sample traces (Anna) — due Nov 13.
A3) Redwood SEs: prepare a short technical pre-read on prefix caching/exported audit logs (Marissa, Monica) — due Nov 15.
A4) Schedule: confirm deep-dive workshop for Nov 18 09:00–10:30 PT (Diego) — pending calendar confirmation.
